sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: N-Queens is a classic **backtracking** problem: place N queens on an N × N board so that no two share a row, column, or diagonal.
items: Try placing a queen **row by row**, exactly one per row
If a square is outside every placed queen's [[primary|attack range]], place it tentatively and recurse to the next row
If the next row has no valid square, **backtrack**: remove the queen and try the next position
Filling all N rows yields one **solution**

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: Backtracking searches all possible placements, but **pruning** abandons most invalid branches early.
items: **Time complexity**: [[danger|O(N!)]] in the worst case, since available squares shrink row by row
**Space complexity**: [[success|O(N)]] — only the column of each row's queen is stored
The real work is far below N! because conflicting branches are pruned very early

sections.heading: What It Optimizes
sections.content: Conflict checking is the hot spot, and a good data structure speeds it up greatly.
items: **Set marking**: track used columns, main diagonals (row - col), and anti-diagonals (row + col) in three sets, making the check [[success|O(1)]]
**Bit operations**: bitmasks for occupancy are a faster advanced technique
Exploit **left-right symmetry**: search only half the first-row choices and mirror, saving about half the time
